AI 예측 시뮬레이션 (실험적)

이 표는 과거 시그널·가격 패턴으로 학습한 실험적 머신러닝 모델이 향후 30일간의 추세 점수를 추정한 것입니다 — 위의 매수/HOLD/매도 판정(기계적 규칙 기반)과는 완전히 별개이며, 어떤 경우에도 그 판정을 대체하거나 바꾸지 않습니다.

추세 점수 = log((매수일수+1) / (매도일수+1)) — 양수면 신고점 갱신(매수)이 트레일링 스탑 하회(매도)보다 많다는 뜻이고, 음수면 그 반대입니다.
왜 대부분 음수로 나오는가: 매수는 그날 하루 20일/100일 최고가를 새로 갱신해야만 발동하는 뾰족한 이벤트인 반면, 매도는 트레일링 스탑(최근 고점 − 3×ATR) 아래로 한 번 내려가면 가격이 다시 회복할 때까지 여러 날 계속 유지되는 상태입니다 — 그래서 12개 자산군 거의 전부 과거 전체 기간에서 매도로 분류된 날이 매수로 분류된 날보다 훨씬 많습니다. 이 점수가 음수라는 사실 자체는 이상 신호가 아니라 구조적으로 당연한 결과이며, 그 자산 자신의 과거 평균 점수보다 지금 예측이 더 높은지/낮은지가 실제로 의미 있는 비교입니다.

"신뢰도"는 검증 구간에서 단순 평균 예측 대비 오차(MAE)가 얼마나 줄었는지를 나타내며, 수치가 낮다고 예측이 틀렸다는 뜻은 아니지만 참고용 이상으로 받아들이지 마세요.

BTC-USD(평균보다 높음), DBA(평균보다 높음), DBB(평균보다 높음), DBC(평균보다 높음), GLD(평균보다 높음), IEF(평균보다 낮음), QQQ(평균보다 낮음), SPY(평균보다 낮음), TLT(평균보다 낮음), UNG(평균보다 낮음), USO(평균보다 높음), UUP(평균보다 높음) 순으로 각 자산의 과거 평균 대비 판정을 확인했다. 전반적으로 원자재·곡물·귀금속·달러 등 실물·대체 자산군(DBA, DBB, DBC, GLD, USO, UUP)과 비트코인이 과거 평균보다 추세 점수가 높아 매도 압력 완화 또는 상대적 강세 성향을 보이는 반면, 주식(QQQ, SPY)과 장기·중기 국채(IEF, TLT), 천연가스(UNG)는 과거 평균보다 점수가 낮아 매도 신호 우위 또는 상대적 약세 성향이 뚜렰하다. 경기민감 자산(주식)이 약세 쪽으로 치우치고 안전자산(채권)마저 동반 약세(금리 상승 압력)를 보이는 가운데 달러와 실물자산이 상대적 강세를 유지하는 패턴은, 통상적인 경기 사이클상 후기 확장기에서 수축기로 넘어가는 전환기(스태그플레이션적 성격이 가미된 후반부)나 공급 측 충격이 수요 둔화와 맞물리는 국면에서 종종 관찰되는 자산 간 디커플링 양상과 유사한 특징을 보인다. 이는 어디까지나 현재 실험적 모델이 포착한 자산군 간 상대적 패턴에 대한 참고적 해석일 뿐, 특정 자산의 향후 가격이나 방향성을 예단하는 것이 아니며 기계적 매매 규칙을 대체하거나 변경하지 않는다.

Weekly market commentary | BlackRock Investment Institute
blackrock-investment-institute · 2026-07-28T01:14:50.812Z

Summary: The BlackRock Weekly Market Commentary emphasizes a nuanced, selective approach to AI-driven equity themes. Key takeaways: - U.S. equities look not expensive on forward P/E, but CAPE valuations remain rich due to expectations of extraordinary earnings growth from massive AI buildouts. - Cheaper AI models shift the winners toward AI infrastructure and scarcity (e.g., data center infra, power and other AI-related infrastructure) rather than the increasingly competitive model layer. - The pace and returns of AI investments hinge on hyperscalers’ capital spending, capital discipline, and the deployment of lower-cost models on cloud platforms; Alphabet’s recent free cash flow decline highlights financing sensitivity. - For the broader economy, AI costs and AI sovereignty (model routing/selection) shape corporate returns and investment strategies; greater competition could alter winners but not the overall AI investment case. - The team remains overweight AI, but with selective, active positioning—favoring infrastructure and scarcity themes around AI rather than chasing long-term model-layer dominance. - Geopolitical and macro risks (Middle East conflict, new tariffs, higher oil prices) have temporarily pushed risk-free yields higher and tech equities under pressure, including a Nasdaq pullback after Alphabet’s capex news. Relevance to Nasdaq/tech stock outlook: - The analysis suggests tech stock performance will be driven by AI capital allocation, returns on AI infrastructure, and the ability to monetize AI adoption while managing higher costs and sovereignty considerations. - Expect more stock-selective, event-driven moves rather than broad-based tech rallies; focus on AI infrastructure exposure and companies/segments with clear cost discipline and scalable AI deployment.

Oversold conditions may persist in a bearish stretch; meaningful long-term bottoms often form only after sentiment extreme, historically down toward RSI near 18. - Fundamental context: The AI megacycle remains intact in terms of demand drivers (cloud growth, enterprise AI adoption, data-center expansion), and the longer-term AI thesis is not broken. Valuation and timing are the main challenges, not an outright collapse. - Risk/reward take: Avoid aggressive buying of dips too early; maintain a patient, disciplined approach. Tactical dip buying may be attractive only after a clearer risk-reward setup (e.g., successful retest of broken support or a stronger sentiment reset). - operator guidance: Focus on earnings guidance, broader market participation, and whether AI spending remains sustainable for names like Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, and Apple. Until those confirmations appear, treat the previous support as resistance and watch for a more extreme sentiment bottom before committing more capital. Bottom line: The Nasdaq tech stock outlook is cautiously bearish in the near term due to a breakdown and rising downside risk, but the longer-term AI narrative remains intact. Trade with patience, wait for stronger technical or fundamental confirmation, and avoid chasing early rebounds.

Top 3 catalysts for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 indices this week
invezz.com · 2026-07-27T00:00:00.000Z

Nasdaq tech stock market outlook (as of this week) - Key drivers for Nasdaq 100 (QQQ) and tech: Earnings beats so far (avg earnings growth ~37.9% vs ~23.6% expected) support tech optimism, with long-duration tech most sensitive to real-rate moves. Next wave of mega-caps (MSFT, AAPL, AMZN, META) could re-rate the index if guidance holds. - Fed impact: The primary overhang. A no-hike or slower-hikes scenario would likely boost QQQ due to its exposure to long-duration tech; a clear higher-for-longer path would push up real yields and weigh on tech multiples. - Specific risks: If the Fed confirms a rate-hike trajectory, or if inflation expectations rise (e.g., due to crude/gasoline pressures from the US-Iran tensions), long-duration tech could underperform. - S&P 500 context (SPY): Broader cyclicals and financials, plus war-driven inflation pressure (gasoline), may cap earnings quality and lift discount rates. A sustained risk-on rally would require inflation to cool and the Fed to turn more dovish. - Earnings outlook: With earnings season intensifying—banks (Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, BofA, Wells Fargo) and tech names (Alphabet, Tesla, Netflix) reporting—earnings growth is a key near-term driver. Strong results help support equity risk appetite despite higher rates. - US-Iran war backdrop: Updates on the conflict influence oil and inflation expectations, which in turn affect Fed policy expectations and market direction. - Market watchlist: Expect reactions around the Fed decision (likely hold vs hike), durable goods, housing data, GDP, and PCE—all pivotal for Nasdaq tech and the broader indices. Bottom line: The Nasdaq tech outlook hinges on continued strong earnings momentum and the Fed path. If the Fed signals slower or no hikes, Nasdaq tech (QQQ) could rebound; if rate hikes resume, long-duration tech multiples may compress. For the S&P 500 (SPY), inflation risk and rate expectations remain the main headwinds unless inflation cools and the Fed pivots dovishly.

Nasdaq, Kospi: Wall Street and Korea markets becoming more intertwined
Lee Ying Shan · 2026-07-28T00:00:00.000Z

Summary: - The Nasdaq and Korea’s Kospi are becoming increasingly correlated as AI spending ties U.S. tech giants to Korean memory-chipmakers (Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix), which dominate the Kospi and sit at the core of AI hardware supply. - The 60-day Kospi–Nasdaq 100 correlation has risen to about 0.50, the strongest since 2021, signaling tighter linkage between U.S. tech stocks and Korean memory plays. - AI hardware demand (especially data-center DRAM) is a key shared driver, with DRAM demand now a majority of global DRAM usage and rising further, reinforcing the links between U.S. hyperscalers and Korean suppliers. - Recent mini-corrections (e.g., July 13) showed both markets retreat together, underscoring the intertwined fate of U.S. tech stocks and Korean memory names like Samsung and SK Hynix. - Analysts warn that the higher correlation reduces diversification benefits: a slowdown in AI/hyperscaler capex could disproportionately impact Korea, given its heavy concentration in a single cyclical theme. - While the linkage is strong now, some expect potential divergence over time due to differences in capital expenditure, product mix, and policy support for domestic chip production. Higher Treasury yields signal new era for interest rates

Summary: - U.S. long-term Treasury yields have surged to multi-year highs, signaling a shift to a higher-for-longer rate regime. - The move is driven by a global shortage of available loanable funds and renewed demand from governments and corporations financing large deficits, AI infrastructure, and other investments—not just inflation fears. - Inflation expectations remain near target, suggesting no immediate Fed policy shift, but sustained higher yields imply ongoing higher policy rates and higher debt service costs for the government. - Mortgage rates and long-duration borrowing are unlikely to fall soon, as higher real and nominal yields persist. - The 10-year breakeven rate sits around 2.28% (below its May peak), while the 10-year yield >4.7% and 30-year TIPS around 2.97%, underscoring a demand-for-long-hold premium beyond inflation alone. - The cost of financing the federal debt could rise meaningfully: every 0.1 percentage point rise in rates could add about $379 billion to interest costs over a decade, with a rough $1.8 trillion impact if current moves persist. - The shift represents a structural change: bond pricing increasingly reflects supply-and-demand dynamics for a finite pool of fundable money, rather than primarily inflation/fed policy signals. Bottom line: - If higher yields endure, expect slower declines in mortgage and other long-term borrowing costs, higher government debt service, and a potentially higher-for-longer interest-rate environment with implications for housing, corporate borrowing, and fiscal policy.

Wood Mackenzie Mid-Year Outlook: Oil and Gas Industry
Wood Mackenzie · 2026-07-28T00:00:00.000Z

Wood Mackenzie’s mid-year outlook suggests a cautious but cash-rich oil and gas sector in 2026: - Global upstream cash flow: Up to about US$495 billion in 2026 if Brent averages US$90/bbl (vs. about US$60/bbl planning assumption). The 49 largest IOCs/NOCs collectively account for ~US$272 billion of this windfall (roughly 70% of their projected investments). - Capex and returns: Despite higher prices, budgets largely unchanged. Companies are maintaining shareholder return plans, with buybacks anticipated to be down ~5% YoY in 2026. Much of the windfall is staying on balance sheets to deleverage rather than be deployed. - Production outlook: A decade-scale decline challenge is evident. About 155 tracked companies face an average 30% production decline from 2030 to 2040 (roughly 32 million boe/d), with over 70 facing declines of 50%+ by 2040. - Spending discipline: Upstream development spend is forecast to dip slightly for the second consecutive year. Focus remains on maintenance, optimization, and low-capital activities rather than large new projects. - Supply and geopolitics: Global oil output is forecast to fall at least 3% in 2026, with significant regional disruption. In the Middle East, Iraq is hit hardest (up to ~3 million bpd offline). LNG supply is also expected to drop by at least 2% (Qatar affected). The overall supply picture has deteriorated amid ongoing conflicts. - Middle East importance: Remains central for portfolio renewal due to scale and cost advantage, despite near-term disruption. - Strategic takeaway: The current price surge is driven more by geopolitics than demand. Companies’ balance sheets are strong, but boards may feel pressure to deploy capital if prices hold in H2; decisions on buybacks, M&A, or new investments will shape 2027 strategy. If you’re analyzing commodity market implications, key takeaways are tighter capital discipline despite a windfall, persistent production decline pressures out to 2040, and geopolitically driven price dynamics influencing whether firms redeploy cash or prioritize balance-sheet strength. For deeper insight, see Wood Mackenzie’s full report (Cash-rich but capital-cautious) via Lens for 49 IOCs/NOCs.

Energy shock: why oil and gas prices have risen less than ...
European Central Bank · 2026-07-27T13:22:57.069Z

Key takeaways on natural gas price outlook (macro analysis): - 2026 gas price response to shocks has been more muted than historical norms. TTF prices rose ~53% to €49/MWh by early June, less than the ~81% rise suggested by past patterns and the ~79% seen during Ukraine war. - The milder reaction is driven by precautionary demand shocks rather than actual supply losses, and Europe’s direct dependence on Middle Eastern LNG remains limited. - LNG competition dynamics: In 2022 Europe diverted LNG to its market due to tight hydropower/nuclear and aggressive bidding. In 2026, the JKM–TTF spread turned positive, signaling weaker LNG rerouting to Europe and a reduced price spike, aided by: - Greater demand flexibility - Gas-to-coal substitution - China’s diversified energy mix - Weaker Asia-wide LNG demand than in 2022 - Overall, lower competition for LNG shipments and adaptable energy demand have helped cap global gas price pressures despite disruptions affecting LNG trade. - Important caveats: price paths still depend on: - Strait of Hormuz developments (supply risk and market sentiment) - Potential prolonged disruption or rapid resolution - How quickly markets replace disrupted supply with LNG and other sources - Inventory levels and economic activity affecting demand Bottom line: In 2026, macro-driven factors—expectations of swift crisis resolution, robust pre-crisis fundamentals, and flexible Asian demand—have subdued natural gas price increases relative to past shocks. A sustained disruption or closure of key choke points could reverse this, while a sustained reopening could push prices downward, especially if supply surpluses persist.
